text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-All yields on treasury bills issued by the Bank of Lebanon fell.

-Parliament speaker Berri says fact that all 15 radio and television stations licensed under new audiovisual media law are owned by officials is a problem because no opposition-owned stations were licensed.
-Palestinian delegation discussed security of refugee camps in Lebanon and future of refugees in light of the Arab-Israeli peace process with officials in Beirut.

-Judicial authorities detain police who shot dead a Palestinian on Sunday accused of belonging to a gang charged with making up to 15 bln Lebanese pounds ($10 million) by selling forged and genuine finance ministry revenue stamps.
-Chinese delegation discussed trade with ministry of economy and trade.
-Prime Minister Hariri discussed with U.S. ambassador Jones preparations for "Friends of Lebanon conference" in Washington on December 16.

-Hizbollah declined comment on reports about the return of German security official Bernd Schmidbauer to Lebanon to continue tracing missing Israeli airman Ron Arad who was shot down over Lebanon in 1986.
-The new cabinet presents policy statement today to parliament.
-Israeli President Weizman visited Israeli occupied zone in south Lebanon
